studies.Study: Park YJ et al. (2026) [PMID: 42361543] — estimate 1 · Male and female
studies.Reference: Association between L-α-glycerylphosphorylcholine use and risk of kidney cancer: A nationwide representative retrospective cohort study.
studies.Title: Association between L-α-glycerylphosphorylcholine use and risk of kidney cancer: A nationwide representative retrospective cohort study.
studies.Authors: Park YJ, Yu J, Kang JH, Park SJ, Jeong S, Lee G, Shin HY, Park SM
studies.Population: Adults aged 50 years or older who underwent health screening in 2009-2010

cases.excerpt: Incident kidney cancer events were identified from 2011 to 2024. α-GPC use was not associated with kidney cancer risk (adjusted HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.84-1.08; 280 events in α-GPC users, 1570 in non-users).
cases.location: Abstract, results; cases derived from reported group counts 280 + 1570 = 1850

effect_size.excerpt: α-GPC use was not associated with kidney cancer risk (adjusted HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.84-1.08; 280 events in α-GPC users, 1570 in non-users).

confidence_interval.excerpt: α-GPC use was not associated with kidney cancer risk (adjusted HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.84-1.08; 280 events in α-GPC users, 1570 in non-users).

design.excerpt: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study

timing.excerpt: Incident kidney cancer events were identified from 2011 to 2024.

continent.excerpt: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The oncologic safety of supplemental α-GPC remains uncertain

gender.excerpt: Results were consistent across lag-time sensitivity analyses and subgroup analyses by age, sex, income, Charlson comorbidity index, and estimated glomerular filtration rate.
